question: What is the SI unit for measuring the electric potential difference between two points in an electric circuit carrying some current?
solution:
The correct answer is **Volt.**** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The SI unit of Electric Potential Difference is Volt. 
 
• **Electric potential Difference** is an external work needed to bring **a unit charge from one location to another under the influence of an electric field.**
 
• The unit is named after the renowned scientist** Alessandro Volta.** 
 
• The** Volt **is signified by the letter** V **in physics.
 
• The instrument used for measuring the potential difference between the 2 terminals is called a **Voltmeter. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information __

 
• **Ampere** is the SI unit of the **Electric Current**. 

 
 
• It is measured with an instrument named **Ammeter**.​
 
 
 
• **Ohm** is the SI unit of **Electrical Resistance**. 
 
 
• It is measured with an instrument named **Ohmmeter.**
 
 
 
• **Joule** is the SI unit of **Work Done. **
 
 
• **​**It is measured with the help of a formula that is a product of force and displacement.
 
 

a1
